accuracy.evidence: Checked against DfE English Appendix 2: Year 1 'joining words and joining clauses using and' with the terms word, sentence, punctuation, full stop and capital letter; Year 2 co-ordination using or, and, but and commas to separate items in a list; conjunction listed as a Year 3 pupil term, so the kid text says joining word and the adult text says when conjunction arrives. The lab lowers the capital of the second clause on joining but keeps 'I' (it is a pronoun always written as a capital); the Oxford comma is described as optional rather than wrong.

misconceptions.evidence: Wrong drops and challenge options are the KS1 slips teachers report: 'and' placed before both items or at the end, the first full stop left in ('I ran. and I jumped'), a lower-case 'i' after joining, 'and' between every item of a list, joining two unrelated ideas, the 'and then… and then' chain, and the opposite slip of sentences run together with no full stop or 'and'.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagand is built around the conjunction itself: a draggable 'and' chip with drop slots between words, joining two sentences that rewrites the full stop and the next capital live, two list slots that accept only comma-then-and, a coherence choice after 'and', and tappable 'and' tiles that split a chain into sentences. flagstop (capitals and end marks) and flagsent (whole sentences) share no mechanism; the 30 percent code-shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the rules by trying: a misplaced 'and' shows in red with a message naming what it now says ('and cats dogs'), a correct join prints the new single sentence with one full stop and says why 'The' became 'the' or why 'I' stayed, an 'and' in the first list box is refused with 'Save and for the last thing', and splitting the chain prints the short sentences side by side.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: Two full stops after joining, 'Between every thing' for and in a list, and 'Yes, long is best' for a chain of ands. The task straight after each one disproves the wrong option, and the done message states whether the guess held.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with nine tagged wrong answers, each with its own message: and in the wrong spot, full stop left before and, small i, and between every list item, no and before the last item, unrelated ideas, a sentence that stops after and, a chain of ands, and a run-on with no joining word or full stop.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short sentences of mostly one-syllable words with a worked example in each, well inside the family limit checked by validate_lessons. Adult text stays within its limit and uses the precise terms joining word, conjunction, co-ordinating conjunction, clause, co-ordination, statement, proper noun, comma in a list and Oxford comma.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and explanation overlap with every other lesson is under 12 percent. Each kid paragraph teaches one rule with one example; adult paragraphs cover curriculum terms, the grammar, named mistakes and what the lab does, with no stock phrases.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 dark and 360 px Android light screenshots of all six steps show word tiles wrapping cleanly onto two lines, a 64 px 'and' chip, full-width idea cards on the ideas step, and large labelled buttons under the canvas. Real pointer drags on the iPhone viewport joined cats and dogs, joined both sentence pairs including the 'I' case, and were refused with the comma message in the wrong list box.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs found no axe WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme on desktop or iPhone and no console errors. Every canvas action has a labelled button (Put and after cats, Put a comma after a hat, Finish with and I put on my coat, Change and number 1 to a full stop) and the canvas aria-label reads each result aloud.
